newsitem.title: USA: Kansas lawmaker seeks end of local property taxes.
newsitem.headline: Kansas lawmaker seeks end of local property taxes.

text.p: According to Kanasa State Rep. Ed McKechnie, D-Pittsburg, the state has too much government and residents pay too much in property taxes.
He has introduced a measure that could lead to a constitutional change to eliminate property taxes or at least examine local government structure in the state.
"You can't get rid of property taxes unless you get rid of some units of government," McKechnie said in a telephone interview Wednesday.

A case in point is Kansas' 105 counties, he said. The proliferation of counties resulted from an 1890s decision that every court house should be a "horseback ride" away so judges would not have to pay for lodging, McKechnie explained.
"We're heading into the 21st Century. Do we still need court houses a horseback ride away?" he asked.

McKechnie said his measure, which requires a two-thirds vote of the legislature, would place a referendum on the November 1998 ballot calling for a constitutional convention solely on taxes and local governments.
If passed by voters, a subsequent election would be held in April 1999 to elect delegates to the convention, which would be held in July, he said.
Any changes adopted by the delegates would need to be approved by voters, he added.
McKechnie said he does not expect his measure to pass, but he hopes it will raise awareness about the hundreds of local taxing bodies in the state.
